key_evidence_spans: A 65-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and bronchial asthma presented with mild headaches
Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a well-defined, 19-mm mass in the left parietal bone
MRI showed the lesion to be isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images, with multiple internal hyperintense foci
the hyperintense foci on T1 images were presumed to represent bone marrow fat
the preserved trabecular architecture suggested that pre-existing structures were not destroyed
with sparse but preserved trabeculae and a slight bony bulge, without disruption of the inner or outer tables
heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images, and restricted diffusion
